copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Tuesday, late-night UTC kickoff, brings Iraq and Norway together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Iraq side, by +10.8pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

Public Elo rates Norway 220 points higher than the other side (Iraq 1540, Norway 1760). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Iraq to win at 18%, the draw at 17%, and Norway to win at 65%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Iraq to win at 8%, the draw at 14%, and Norway to win at 76%. On the Iraq side specifically the market reads 8%, which prices out at American odds of +1233. Compared against the model's 18%, that's the +10.8pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Iraq the lower bound is 14%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +6.4pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Iraq priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 25 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the Iraq side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Iraq a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +10.8pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
copy.summary: Iraq enter as the longshot — Polymarket prices their chances at 8%. The model rates them at 18%, a +10.8pp disagreement and one of our widest in this competition.
copy.title: Iraq v Norway · the model leans Iraq
